theme: Dependency graphs: target dependencies and cycles

terms.definition: A link that says one target needs another target, so the other target must build first.
terms.example: Add the target dependency, then build again.
terms.code:
import PackageDescription
let app = Target.target(
    name: "App",
    dependencies: ["Networking"])

terms.definition: A map of all the modules in a project and which ones depend on each other.
terms.example: Draw the dependency graph before the refactor.

terms.definition: A loop where module A needs module B and module B also needs module A, so neither can build first.
terms.example: A circular dependency stops the build.
terms.code:
let deps = ["A": ["B"], "B": ["A"]]
let loop = deps["A"]?.contains("B") == true
    && deps["B"]?.contains("A") == true
print(loop ? "cycle" : "ok")

video.description:
Learn to explain how modules depend on each other and how to fix a build loop: Target Dependency, Dependency Graph & Circular Dependency, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Target Dependency - A link that says one target needs another target, so the other target must build first.
Dependency Graph - A map of all the modules in a project and which ones depend on each other.
Circular Dependency - A loop where module A needs module B and module B also needs module A, so neither can build first.

landscape.title: iOS Target Dependency, Dependency Graph & Circular Dependency | Day 250
landscape.description:
Explain Target Dependency, Dependency Graph & Circular Dependency in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Target Dependency, Dependency Graph, Circular Dependency 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Target Dependency - A link that says one target needs another target, so the other target must build first.
한국어: Target Dependency: 한 타깃이 다른 타깃을 필요로 해서 그 타깃이 먼저 빌드되어야 함을 나타내는 연결

Dependency Graph - A map of all the modules in a project and which ones depend on each other.
한국어: Dependency Graph: 프로젝트의 모든 모듈과 어떤 모듈이 서로 의존하는지를 보여 주는 지도

Circular Dependency - A loop where module A needs module B and module B also needs module A, so neither can build first.
한국어: Circular Dependency: 모듈 A가 B를 필요로 하고 B도 A를 필요로 해서 어느 쪽도 먼저 빌드할 수 없는 순환

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about a package build that fails because two targets need each other, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Target Dependency, Dependency Graph and Circular Dependency in English?

dialogue.title: The build that loops
dialogue.setting: A package that will not build

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, Swift Package Manager cannot build our package, and I do not understand why.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's look at the target dependency in `ui`. A target dependency says one target needs another.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. That is a target dependency, and the build order follows it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But `core` also lists `UI` in its dependencies.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There is your problem. That is a circular dependency, and neither target can build first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How can I find these problems early?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Draw the dependency graph. A dependency graph is a map of who depends on whom.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like a diagram with arrows from `ui` to `core`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A healthy dependency graph has arrows in one direction only.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So we remove the target dependency from `core` to `UI`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Move the shared code to a third target, and the circular dependency is gone.
